facts.t: Indian municipal revenue is a fifth of the global norm
facts.d: Municipal revenues amount to roughly 1% of GDP, against 5–6% in Brazil and South Africa. Property tax recovery is starker still — about 0.2% of GDP here, against 1–2.5% in comparable economies.

facts.t: Only eleven Indian cities have ever issued municipal bonds
facts.d: They have been legally permitted for decades. Pune and Ahmedabad demonstrated that infrastructure can be financed without waiting for grants — yet almost no Tier-2 or Tier-3 city has followed, mostly for want of credit ratings and audited accounts.

facts.t: Indore has won Swachh Survekshan six times running
facts.d: The formula was unglamorous: complete door-to-door segregated collection and a bio-CNG plant converting wet waste to fuel. It is the standard counter-example to the claim that Indian municipal service delivery cannot be fixed.

bank.q: Municipal revenues in India are approximately what share of GDP?
bank.e: About 1%, compared with 5–6% in Brazil and South Africa. The 0.2% figure refers specifically to property tax recovery.

bank.q: With reference to the 74th Amendment framework, consider the following statements:
s: District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees are defunct or unformed in most states.
Only fourteen states held regular municipal elections in the last five years.
Municipal functions are often exercised through parastatals and parallel bodies.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they describe why the 74th Amendment's promise remains largely unrealised.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a cause of fragmented municipal functions?
o: Jal Boards reporting to state governments rather than urban local bodies
Smart City special purpose vehicles diluting municipal authority
Full operationalisation of the eighteen Twelfth Schedule functions
Overlapping jurisdictions in waste, housing and water
bank.e: The Twelfth Schedule functions have not been fully operationalised — doing so via exclusive activity maps is the proposed remedy.

bank.as: Urban local bodies lost fiscal autonomy after GST.
bank.rs: Local levies such as octroi and entry tax were subsumed into the new regime.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — which is why property tax reform and municipal bonds recur in every urban finance proposal.

bank.q: Match List I (city or institution) with List II (achievement):
pairs: 1. Municipal bonds funding infrastructure without aid delays
2. E-learning combined with site visits for municipal staff
bank.e: Indore for sanitation, Pune and Ahmedabad for bonds, Surat and Pune for real-time reporting, and the Odisha Urban Academy for staff training.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about municipal functionaries:
s: The deputation model weakens continuity in city management.
Most cities lack trained town planners, so planning is outsourced to consultants.
The commissioner-led model strengthens the authority of elected councils.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The commissioner-led model does the opposite — it limits the authority of elected councils.

bank.q: The Twelfth Schedule lists how many functions for urban local bodies?
bank.e: Eighteen. Twenty-nine is the number in the Eleventh Schedule for panchayats.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed municipal finance reforms EXCEPT:
o: GIS-linked property records and digital tax platforms
Institutional credit ratings and pooled bonds for smaller cities
Increasing dependence on tied central grants
Skill-milestone incentives within the City Finance Index
bank.e: Dependence on tied grants is the problem being solved, not a reform.

bank.q: With reference to service delivery, consider the following statements:
s: More than 45% of urban local bodies miss service-level benchmarks in water and waste.
Tier-II and Tier-III cities carry the largest backlogs.
A dedicated Municipal Services Cadre is proposed.
bank.e: All three are correct — the proposed cadre would bring urban planners and engineers into permanent municipal service.

bank.q: Which mechanism is proposed to give citizens statutory standing in city governance?
bank.e: Ward Sabhas with statutory powers, alongside mandatory online disclosure of budgets, resolutions and social audits.
